Gov. Kemp issues state of emergency for Georgia ahead of Hurricane Isaias
Governor Brian Kemp has declared a statewide emergency ahead of Hurricane Isaias' expected arrival this weekend. Officials urge residents across all 159 counties to prepare for possible severe weather including strong winds and flooding.
Governor Brian P. Kemp issued an updated State of Emergency for all 159 counties in Georgia on Oct. 8 in preparation for Hurricane Isaias. The Executive Order allows emergency management teams to arrange and position resources before the storm’s expected impact, and directs the Georgia Emergency Management and Homeland Security Agency (GEMA/HS) to activate the State Operations Center beginning early Friday afternoon.
"As we always do with weather events, we’re hoping for the best but preparing for the worst," said Governor Brian Kemp. "I encourage all Georgians to take this storm seriously and prepare now by stocking up on food, batteries, flashlights, water, and other necessities in case of severe weather impacting communities Friday night through Saturday."
Forecasters expect Hurricane Isaias to make landfall on the Gulf Coast Friday evening, with potential impacts continuing through Saturday across Georgia. These may include strong wind gusts, heavy rain leading to flooding, spin-off tornadoes, downed trees, and power lines.
"As we closely monitor this system, ensuring the safety of all Georgians is our top priority,” said GEMA/HS Director Josh Lamb. “That's why GEMA/HS is working around the clock in coordination with local, state, and federal partners to ensure that we are fully prepared for any potential impacts. All parts of the state could see impacts from this storm, and we have the resources ready to assist them if that is the case."
Officials advise residents not to drive or walk through standing water or around barricades during flooding conditions and warn against approaching downed power lines due to risk of electric shock or electrocution. In case a tornado warning is issued, residents are advised that storm cellars or basements offer optimal protection; if unavailable, a small windowless interior room or hallway on a building’s lowest floor should be used.
The Government of Georgia's authority extends across all counties within the state as part of its executive branch operations based in Atlanta at the Governor's Mansion—a Greek Revival-style residence built in 1967—according to the official website. The Georgia Emergency Management and Homeland Security Agency collaborates with local governments as well as private sector partners through initiatives such as Ready Georgia aimed at disaster preparedness.
